title: CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026: Call for Applications for 10 PhD Candidates at German Universities
summary: The CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026 is now accepting applications from qualified candidates interested in pursuing doctoral research in agricultural sciences and related interdisciplinary fields at a German university. The scholarship provides an opportunity for researchers with an MSc degree to develop a PhD project connected to ongoing CGIAR++ research activities and to work under joint supervision from a senior CGIAR++ scientist and a professor affiliated with a German university. For the 2026 call, the Hub plans to support 10 PhD candidates . The previous call in 2025 attracted a high volume of qualified applications and had an acceptance rate of just 5% , highlighting the competitive nature of the opportunity. The application deadline for the current call is 30 November 2026 . CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026 Overview The programme is designed for candidates who want to undertake doctoral research that contributes to existing CGIAR++ research activities. A particularly important feature of the scholarship is its collaborative structure: applicants cannot apply independently without first establishing the required academic and research partnerships. Each accepted candidate must form a “tridem” consisting of: The PhD candidate. A senior CGIAR++ scientist. A professor affiliated with a German university. These three parties are expected to work together to develop the scientific proposal and establish the supervision and research arrangements required for the PhD. The PhD project must also be connected to an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity and should provide additional value to that research programme. Deadline for the CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026 Application deadline: 30 November 2026 Applicants should begin preparing their applications well before the deadline because the process requires coordination with both a CGIAR++ senior scientist and a professor affiliated with a German university. The required supervisory and hosting documents must also be prepared and submitted according to the application instructions. Who Can Apply for the CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship? The call is aimed at candidates who already hold an MSc degree in Agricultural Sciences or a related discipline and who meet the academic requirements specified by the programme. Relevant academic backgrounds can include a broad range of disciplines, reflecting the interdisciplinary nature of the research supported by the programme. Examples specifically listed in the call include: Agricultural Sciences Biology Geography Sociology Veterinary Medicine Marine Biology Forestry Political Sciences Law Economics Other related fields Applicants are expected to have achieved an above-average final grade in their MSc degree. Requirements for Non-European Degrees Candidates holding degrees from outside Europe must additionally provide a ranking from the issuing university . This requirement allows the programme to assess the academic standing of qualifications obtained outside the European university system. A Unique Three-Way Research and Supervision Structure One of the most important requirements of the scholarship is that applicants must establish the appropriate research partnership before submitting their application. Only applications from the required “tridems” will be accepted. The tridem consists of: 1. The PhD Candidate The candidate develops and undertakes the proposed doctoral research and must meet the academic requirements of the programme. 2. CGIAR++ Senior Scientist The candidate must work with a senior scientist from a CGIAR++ Center. The scientist serves as the CGIAR++ supervisor and must confirm the candidate s connection to an appropriate CGIAR++ research programme or project. 3. Professor at a German University The candidate must also identify a professor affiliated with a German university who will jointly supervise the doctoral project. The scientific proposal is developed collaboratively by these three parties. This means prospective applicants should not wait until the final stages of the application process to identify their supervisors. Establishing the required research relationships is an essential part of becoming eligible to apply. PhD Research Must Be Connected to CGIAR++ Research Another central requirement is that candidates must be hosted by a CGIAR++ Center . The proposed doctoral research must be attached to an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity . The call indicates that the project is preferably connected to an international, multidisciplinary research project . The proposed PhD research should not simply duplicate existing research. Instead, it should be: Connected to an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity. Complementary to the existing research. Designed to provide additional value to the CGIAR++ research activity. Supported by an appropriate CGIAR++ Center. Developed with the CGIAR++ and German university supervisors. This makes the scholarship particularly relevant to candidates who can demonstrate how their proposed doctoral research fits into a broader research programme. PhD Study at a German University Successful candidates must enroll in a PhD study programme at a German university . However, applicants do not need to be German nationals . The programme therefore provides an opportunity for qualified international candidates to pursue doctoral studies in Germany while maintaining a research connection with a CGIAR++ Center. Applicants from CGIAR++ partner countries are welcome to apply . The call also specifically states that female students are particularly encouraged to apply . Documents Required from Applicants Candidates must prepare several documents as part of their application. 1. Letter of Motivation Applicants must provide a signed letter of motivation . The letter must be: Signed by the applicant. No more than one page. The motivation letter should be prepared carefully because it forms part of the candidate s application package. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a tabular CV . The CV must be: No more than one page. Signed. Dated. Presented in tabular form. Candidates should therefore ensure that their CV follows the format requested by the programme rather than submitting an unnecessarily long academic CV. 3. Research Proposal A research proposal is required. Applicants must use the official research proposal template provided by the programme. Research Proposal Template The proposal should be developed jointly with the required supervisors because the scholarship specifically requires a scientific proposal created through the tridem structure. 4. MSc Certificate and Academic Transcript Applicants must submit: Their MSc certificate. Their transcript of academic records. These documents must be issued by the examination office . Applicants with non-European degrees should also remember the additional requirement concerning university ranking. 5. English Proficiency Certificate Applicants must provide evidence of English-language proficiency. The call accepts: TOEFL IELTS Another English proficiency certificate Candidates should make sure that their proof of English proficiency satisfies the programme s requirements. Documents Required From the Supervisors The application also requires documents from the two supervisory sides of the proposed PhD. These documents must be sent by the respective supervisors as one PDF by email to: hub@landscapealliance.org The supervisor documentation includes three important components. 1. German University Professor s Recommendation and Supervision Confirmation The professor affiliated with a German university must provide: A letter of recommendation. Confirmation of supervision. The programme provides a specific template that should be used. German University Supervisor Template 2. CGIAR++ Scientist Recommendation and Supervision Commitment The CGIAR++ Center scientist must provide: A letter of recommendation. A supervision commitment. Confirmation that the candidate is attached to a relevant CGIAR++ research programme or project. The programme also provides a specific template for this document. CGIAR++ Supervisor Template 3. Hosting Agreement The respective CGIAR++ Center must also provide a Hosting Agreement . This confirms the candidate s intended hosting arrangement with the CGIAR++ Center. The official template is available here: CGIAR++ Hosting Agreement Template All three supervisor-related documents are to be sent together as one PDF to hub@landscapealliance.org . 10 PhD Candidates to Be Supported For the current 2026 call, the Hub is seeking to support 10 PhD candidates . This makes the opportunity highly selective, particularly considering the programme s previous application experience. According to the information provided in the call, the 2025 application round attracted a high volume of qualified applications and had an acceptance rate of 5% . Prospective applicants should therefore pay close attention to the eligibility requirements, research proposal, supervisory arrangements and supporting documentation. What Makes the Research Opportunity Interdisciplinary? The list of eligible academic backgrounds demonstrates that the programme is not limited to traditional agricultural science disciplines. Applicants may come from fields including: Biology Geography Sociology Veterinary Medicine Marine Biology Forestry Political Sciences Law Economics This interdisciplinary approach can be particularly relevant for research addressing complex agricultural, environmental, social, economic, governance or development-related questions. The requirement for the PhD project to complement ongoing CGIAR++ research also means that applicants should consider how their research connects with broader research activities rather than developing an isolated doctoral project. MORE INFO. HERE How to Prepare a Strong Application Because applicants must establish relationships with both a CGIAR++ scientist and a German university professor, preparation should begin early. Step 1: Confirm Your Academic Eligibility First, verify that you have an MSc degree in Agricultural Sciences or an appropriate related field and that your final grade is above average. If your degree was awarded outside Europe, prepare the required university ranking documentation. Step 2: Identify Potential Supervisors You will need both: A senior CGIAR++ scientist. A professor affiliated with a German university. The two supervisors must be able to jointly support the proposed PhD project. Step 3: Develop the Research Idea The research idea should be developed collaboratively with the supervisors. Consider how the proposed research: Fits into existing CGIAR++ research. Complements ongoing work. Adds value to the research programme. Can be undertaken through a German university PhD programme. Benefits from the expertise and research environment of the CGIAR++ Center. Step 4: Prepare the Research Proposal Use the official template rather than creating an unrelated format. Because the proposal is central to the application, applicants should ensure that the proposed research is clearly connected to the ongoing CGIAR++ activity identified by the supervisors. Step 5: Collect Academic Documents Prepare your: MSc certificate. Academic transcript. University ranking, if applicable. English proficiency certificate. Step 6: Prepare the Personal Documents The motivation letter and CV must comply with the specified format. The motivation letter has a maximum length of one page, while the CV must also be no more than one page and must be signed and dated. Step 7: Coordinate the Supervisor Documents The German university professor and CGIAR++ scientist must complete their respective documents, while the CGIAR++ Center must provide the Hosting Agreement. These documents must be combined into one PDF and sent by the supervisors to hub@landscapealliance.org . Application Deadline The deadline for the current CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship call is: 30 November 2026 Since the application requires collaboration among the candidate, CGIAR++ scientist and German university professor, candidates should not leave the preparation of the application until the final days before the deadline. How to Apply Applicants should begin with the official Call for Applications and follow the programme s application instructions and templates. Call for Applications The current call is specifically seeking 10 PhD candidates . Candidates should ensure that all required personal, academic, research and supervisory documentation is prepared before submission. Key Information at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship Level PhD Field Agricultural Sciences and related disciplines Study location Germany Research connection Ongoing CGIAR++ research activity Number of candidates 10 Required degree MSc Supervision CGIAR++ senior scientist + German university professor Research structure Required three-way “tridem” Nationality German nationality not required International applicants Welcome Partner-country applicants Welcome Female applicants Particularly encouraged English requirement TOEFL, IELTS or other English proficiency certificate Application deadline 30 November 2026 Previous acceptance rate 5% in the 2025 call Important Points Applicants Should Remember Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully check the following: You must have an MSc degree in Agricultural Sciences or a related field. Your final grade should be above average. Non-European degree holders must provide a ranking from their issuing university. You must establish the required three-way research partnership. You need a senior CGIAR++ scientist as a supervisor. You need a professor affiliated with a German university as a joint supervisor. Your PhD project must be connected to ongoing CGIAR++ research. You must be hosted by a CGIAR++ Center. Your research should complement and add value to the existing CGIAR++ research activity. You must enroll in a PhD programme at a German university. You must provide the required academic and English-language documentation. Your supervisors must submit their required documents together as one PDF. The complete application process must be completed by 30 November 2026 . Conclusion The CGIAR++ PhD Scholarship 2026 provides an opportunity for qualified MSc graduates to pursue doctoral research at a German university while becoming part of an ongoing CGIAR++ research activity. Its interdisciplinary eligibility criteria make the programme relevant to applicants from agricultural sciences as well as fields such as biology, geography, sociology, forestry, veterinary medicine, political sciences, law and economics. A distinctive feature of the opportunity is its required tridem structure , bringing together the PhD candidate, a senior CGIAR++ scientist and a professor affiliated with a German university. The proposed doctoral research must also be connected to an existing CGIAR++ research programme and demonstrate additional value to that work. With only 10 PhD candidates being supported in the current call and a reported 5% acceptance rate in the 2025 call , applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements, research proposal and supervisory documentation. Qualified candidates should begin developing their research proposal and establishing the required supervisory relationships well before the 30 November 2026 deadline. title: UNDP Paid Internships 2026 for Students and Graduates – Launch Your Global Development Career
summary: Are you passionate about world development and are looking for valuable experiences to complement your studies? The UNDP Internship Program is an outstanding opportunity where interns have the chance to learn about the leading development programs initiated by the United Nations. The UNDP Internship program aims to provide candidates interested in international development with a deeper knowledge of the UNDP’s work. The UNDP Internship is an excellent opportunity for individuals who are interested in hands-on experience with issues related to global poverty eradication and sustainable development. UNDP offers attractive paid positions in several areas for the sole purpose of promoting global development. Around 170 countries are part of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), which is the leading development promotion agency of the UN. UNDP interns have a tremendous opportunity to gain valuable hands-on experience working with qualified, well-trained, and exceedingly experienced mentors and supervisors to achieve the goals of the UNDP. The organization works towards a better future for humanity by addressing issues such as eradicating poverty, reducing inequities and exclusion, and empowering countries to embark on sustainable development and growth. The UNDP internship program includes students and recent graduates from the most diverse fields of knowledge. The most popular areas of study in this program are Economics, Public or Business Administration, Environmental Studies, International Relations, and Other related areas. The type of activities that interns perform can vary depending on the opening and the needs of the department where they are placed. The following are the most common responsibilities: Conducting research, Writing documents, Cataloguing information, forums, or other collaborative events, Assisting in the organization of conferences, and Publishing knowledge stories/best practices. These internships can take place at the UN’s headquarters, its country offices, or regional offices. The length of an internship depends on both the candidate’s qualifications and the needs of the UN. UNDP Internship Program Details: Host Organization: United Nation Development Program Program Locations: UNDP Country Offices, at Regional Hubs or Headquarters in New York. Internship Type: Full-time/Part-time (Paid) Eligible Countries: All Deadline: Varies What are the Benefits of the UNDP Internship Program? The UNDP interns would receive a monthly stipend. UNDP interns receive a monthly stipend to cover costs associated with the internship. Stipend amounts can vary from one duty station to another. There are chances that interns will be assigned to UNDP or to the UN system in the future. Additionally, interns may receive financial aid from their nominating institutions or the government. Eligibility Criteria for the UNDP Internships: Applicants from all over the world may apply for the UNDP internships. Candidates can either be enrolled in a graduate program or have earned a second university degree, or they can be in the final academic year of their first university degree. The candidate should have fluency in at least one of UNDP’s three working languages: French, English, and Spanish. The knowledge of Arabic, Portuguese, Russian, or another Eastern European language would be advantageous. The candidates should be able to demonstrate their relevance to UNDP programs. At the time of application, the candidate must be at least 18 years of age. The candidate must demonstrate the ability to work with people from different languages, national, and cultural backgrounds. Deadline: The application deadline to apply for the UNDP internship varies according to each internship program. How to Apply for the UNDP Internship Program? Candidates must submit their applications only via UNDP’s website. Internship opportunities at UNDP are listed in the UNDP Job Section. Please select an area of interest and then click “Apply.”. Please ensure that you follow the specific deadline for the internship program, as each internship has a different and exclusive deadline. If you wish to apply to more than one program, you must register separately for each program. title: Green Climate Fund Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group 2027–2030: Call for Nominations for Indigenous Peoples Representatives
summary: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) has opened a call for nominations for its Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group (IPAG) for the 2027–2030 term , providing an opportunity for Indigenous Peoples representatives to contribute to dialogue, coordination, and engagement between Indigenous Peoples, the Green Climate Fund, and its partners on climate action and climate finance. For the 2027–2030 term, the GCF is seeking nominations to fill one vacancy in each of four regions: Africa, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Pacific . The nomination process is specifically designed as an Indigenous Peoples-led self-selection process , meaning nominations are expected to come through relevant Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, organizations, networks, and regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses. The call is particularly relevant to Indigenous Peoples organizations and representatives working on climate action, environmental issues, Indigenous Peoples rights, sustainable development, climate finance, community development, and related areas . Nomination deadline: 9 October 2026 About the Green Climate Fund Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group The Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group (IPAG) was established under the Green Climate Fund s Indigenous Peoples Policy to strengthen coordination and engagement between Indigenous Peoples and the Green Climate Fund and its partners. The group provides a mechanism through which Indigenous Peoples perspectives can be brought into the GCF s work. Its membership consists of Indigenous Peoples representatives from regions of developing States where the Green Climate Fund may fund activities. Rather than being an ordinary employment position, IPAG membership is part of the GCF s broader institutional approach to Indigenous Peoples participation and engagement. The current call follows recommendations arising from the eighth meeting of the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group , after which the GCF Secretariat began the process of filling vacancies for the next 2027–2030 term. What Is the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group? The Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group is a mechanism for strengthening interaction between the Green Climate Fund and Indigenous Peoples. This is particularly significant in the context of climate action because Indigenous Peoples and their communities are frequently closely connected to land, forests, water, biodiversity, natural resources, and ecosystems that are affected by climate change and climate-related interventions. Through IPAG, Indigenous Peoples representatives can participate in a structured advisory mechanism connecting Indigenous Peoples perspectives with the GCF and its partners. The group therefore provides an avenue for Indigenous Peoples institutions and representatives to contribute perspectives relevant to climate action, inclusion, environmental sustainability, and the interests and concerns of Indigenous Peoples in developing regions. Regional Vacancies for the 2027–2030 Term For the 2027–2030 IPAG term, the Green Climate Fund has identified four regional vacancies . There is one vacancy in each of the following regions : 1. Africa Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, organizations, networks, and regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses in Africa may submit nominations for the African regional vacancy. The nominee should be an Indigenous Peoples representative from a developing State where the GCF may fund activities . 2. Eastern Europe and Central Asia The second vacancy is for the Eastern Europe and Central Asia region. Relevant Indigenous Peoples institutions and organizations in this region may nominate an appropriate Indigenous Peoples representative who meets the requirements and considerations established in the IPAG Terms of Reference. 3. Latin America and the Caribbean The third vacancy covers Latin America and the Caribbean. Indigenous Peoples institutions, organizations, networks, and regional caucuses may participate in the self-selection process by submitting qualified nominations for this regional position. 4. Pacific The fourth vacancy is for the Pacific region. Indigenous Peoples organizations and institutions from eligible developing States in the Pacific may submit nominations for consideration. The GCF notes that where no eligible nomination is received from one of these four regions, the Secretariat may consider eligible nominations from underrepresented sub-regions or groups , consistent with advice from the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group. Who Can Be Nominated? This opportunity is specifically focused on Indigenous Peoples representatives rather than applicants from the general public. The nominee should be a representative from an Indigenous Peoples institution, organization, body, network, or related structure in an eligible developing State where the Green Climate Fund may fund activities. Importantly, individuals do not simply submit a personal application independently. The nomination must come through an appropriate Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization. The nominating organization must also formally confirm that the individual has been nominated or endorsed by the organization s head or designated focal point. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to individuals who already have an established connection with Indigenous Peoples organizations or representative structures. What Experience Should the Nominee Demonstrate? The nomination must include a statement demonstrating how the nominee satisfies the criteria and factors for IPAG membership contained in the group s Terms of Reference. The nomination should also include a short CV or biography highlighting the nominee s experience and contributions that are relevant to areas such as: Indigenous Peoples issues Climate action Environmental issues Climate-related development Community-level initiatives Indigenous Peoples participation Related areas of relevance to the work of the Green Climate Fund The GCF specifically requests that the nominee s relevant experience and contributions be clearly presented. This means that a generic CV may not be sufficient on its own. The information submitted should help demonstrate the nominee s connection to Indigenous Peoples issues and/or climate action and explain why the person is appropriate for representation on the Advisory Group. Nomination Must Come From an Indigenous Peoples Organization One of the most important aspects of this call is that it is an organization-led nomination process . Individuals interested in being considered should therefore first establish whether an eligible Indigenous Peoples institution, organization, body, network, or regional caucus is able and willing to formally nominate or endorse them. The nominating organization is responsible for providing information about itself and the nominee and for confirming that the nomination is formally supported. The organization must identify the region for which the nomination is being submitted. Information Required From the Nominating Organization The Green Climate Fund has specified the information that must accompany each nomination. 1. Information about the nominating organization The submission should include: The name of the Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization. Contact details of the organization. The region for which the nomination is being submitted. This information allows the GCF to establish the institutional source of the nomination and the relevant regional context. 2. Information about the nominee The submission must provide: The nominee s full name. The nominee s contact details. Email address. Telephone number. The nominee s information should be accurate and current because the nomination process may involve subsequent communication with the individual and the nominating organization. 3. Formal confirmation of nomination or endorsement The nomination must include confirmation from the head or designated focal point of the nominating Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization . This confirmation should establish that the nominee has been formally nominated or endorsed by the organization. This is an important distinction because the opportunity is not structured as an open individual application. 4. Statement demonstrating eligibility and suitability The nominating organization must provide a statement demonstrating how the nominee meets the criteria and factors to be considered for IPAG membership as established in the Terms of Reference. This statement should therefore go beyond simply saying that the person is experienced. It should connect the nominee s experience, knowledge, representation, and contributions to the requirements and considerations for IPAG membership. 5. Short CV or biography The nomination should include a short CV or biography of the nominee. The GCF specifically asks that this document highlight the individual s: Experience relating to Indigenous Peoples issues; Contributions to Indigenous Peoples communities or organizations; Experience in climate action; Relevant experience in related areas. A strong biography should therefore make the nominee s relevant experience immediately clear rather than focusing primarily on unrelated professional achievements. 6. Additional endorsements Endorsements from other Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, or organizations within the respective region are highly encouraged . Although the GCF does not state that these additional endorsements are mandatory, they can form part of the regional self-selection process and demonstrate broader institutional support for the nominee. Organizations considering a nomination may therefore wish to explore whether additional Indigenous Peoples organizations within their region are willing to provide endorsements. How the Indigenous Peoples-Led Self-Selection Process Works The call is based on an Indigenous Peoples-led self-selection process . This means that the selection mechanism is designed to involve Indigenous Peoples institutions and representative structures in identifying nominees for the regional vacancies. The process is therefore different from a conventional recruitment exercise in which individuals compete for a job by submitting applications directly to an employer. The GCF is specifically asking relevant Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, organizations, networks, and regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses to submit nominations. The regional dimension is also important. Each of the four listed regions has one vacancy, and nominations should identify the region for which the nomination is being submitted. What Do IPAG Members Do? The detailed IPAG Terms of Reference describe the group s role and functions, membership arrangements, competencies and factors to be considered, the self-selection process, working arrangements, and provisions relating to revision and termination of the Terms of Reference. The Terms of Reference therefore provide the principal framework for understanding the responsibilities and expectations associated with IPAG membership. Potential nominees and nominating organizations should review the Terms of Reference carefully before preparing a submission. The GCF s announcement specifically directs prospective nominators to the Terms of Reference when demonstrating how a nominee meets the criteria and factors considered for IPAG membership. Is IPAG Membership a Paid Position? No. IPAG members serve on a voluntary and non-remunerated basis . This means that the opportunity should not be treated as a salaried employment position or paid consultancy. However, the GCF indicates that where in-person participation is required, travel-related arrangements may be supported in accordance with applicable GCF policies and procedures . This distinction is important: the membership itself is voluntary and unpaid, but certain travel-related arrangements associated with required in-person participation may receive support under applicable GCF rules. How Often Do IPAG Members Meet? IPAG members can expect to participate in: Two in-person meetings each year Monthly online meetings Additional online meetings where specific activities require them The frequency of participation means that nominees should be prepared to make a sustained commitment throughout the 2027–2030 term. The opportunity is therefore not simply an honorary designation. It involves ongoing participation in the group s work. Working Language The working language of the Green Climate Fund is English . Consequently, nominees should be able to participate in the group s activities within this working-language environment. Organizations preparing nominations should take this into account when identifying and supporting nominees. Duration of the Appointment The call concerns the 2027–2030 term of the Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group. This means that nominees are being considered for participation in the Advisory Group during this multi-year period rather than for a short-term event or one-time consultation. The expected meetings and activities described by the GCF indicate that members should be prepared for continued engagement throughout their term. Important Deadline The deadline for submitting nominations is: 9 October 2026 Nominations must be sent to: IPAGnomination@gcfund.org The Green Climate Fund s official announcement specifies that nomination submissions must reach this email address no later than 9 October 2026 . Organizations should therefore allow sufficient time to identify the nominee, obtain the required organizational confirmation, prepare the supporting statement, compile the nominee s CV or biography, and obtain any additional endorsements they wish to include. How to Prepare a Strong Nomination Organizations interested in submitting a nomination should carefully organize their materials before sending them. Step 1: Identify the relevant regional vacancy First determine whether the nomination relates to: Africa; Eastern Europe and Central Asia; Latin America and the Caribbean; or the Pacific. The nominating organization should clearly identify the region for which the nomination is being submitted. Step 2: Identify an appropriate Indigenous Peoples representative The nominee should have a clear connection to Indigenous Peoples representation and relevant experience. Organizations should consider the individual s experience with Indigenous Peoples issues, climate action, environmental matters, community engagement, and other areas relevant to the IPAG mandate. Step 3: Review the IPAG Terms of Reference Before preparing the nomination statement, the organization should review the official IPAG Terms of Reference. The Terms of Reference explain the role and functions of IPAG, membership, competencies and factors to be considered, the self-selection process, working arrangements, and other institutional provisions. This review is particularly important because the GCF requires the nomination to include a statement demonstrating how the nominee meets the relevant criteria and factors. Step 4: Prepare the nominee s CV or biography The CV or biography should focus attention on experience and contributions relevant to: Indigenous Peoples; climate action; environmental issues; community development; Indigenous representation; and related areas. Relevant achievements should be presented clearly and in a way that demonstrates the nominee s connection to the purpose of the Advisory Group. Step 5: Obtain formal organizational endorsement The organization s head or designated focal point should formally confirm the nomination or endorsement. This confirmation should be included in the submission. Step 6: Consider additional regional endorsements The GCF highly encourages endorsements from other Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies, or organizations in the relevant region. Where appropriate, organizations may therefore seek additional endorsements to demonstrate broader regional support. Step 7: Submit before the deadline The completed nomination should be sent to IPAGnomination@gcfund.org no later than 9 October 2026 . Organizations should avoid leaving the submission until the final day because obtaining organizational confirmation and additional endorsements may require coordination with multiple people. Why This Opportunity Is Significant for Indigenous Peoples Representatives The IPAG nomination process provides a structured avenue for Indigenous Peoples representatives to participate in engagement with one of the major international institutions working on climate finance. The Green Climate Fund is focused on mobilizing and delivering climate finance for developing countries, and its work includes climate-related investments and partnerships across developing regions. The Fund currently reports activities across Africa, Asia and the Pacific, Eastern Europe, Central Asia and the Middle East, and Latin America and the Caribbean. The IPAG mechanism specifically recognizes the importance of Indigenous Peoples participation in this broader climate-finance context. For Indigenous Peoples organizations, therefore, the nomination process is an opportunity to put forward representatives who can contribute perspectives and experience relating to Indigenous Peoples and climate action. Who Should Consider This Opportunity? This call is particularly relevant to: Indigenous Peoples institutions; Indigenous Peoples organizations; Indigenous Peoples representative bodies; Indigenous Peoples networks; regional Indigenous Peoples caucuses; Indigenous Peoples representatives with experience in climate action; Indigenous Peoples representatives working on environmental issues; Indigenous Peoples advocates involved in climate and sustainable-development discussions; and eligible Indigenous Peoples representatives from developing States where the GCF may fund activities. It is important to emphasize that the call is not a general application opportunity open to anyone interested in climate change . The nomination must come through a relevant Indigenous Peoples institution, body, or organization, and the nominee must be an Indigenous Peoples representative from an eligible developing State. Regional and Geographic Eligibility The call specifically identifies four regions: Africa, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Pacific. The nominee should come from a developing State where the Green Climate Fund may fund activities. This means that geographic eligibility is tied to both the four regional vacancies and the GCF s framework concerning developing States where it may finance activities. The GCF s announcement provides a link to its countries and regions information for determining the relevant geographic context. Key Facts at a Glance Opportunity Details Opportunity Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group (IPAG) 2027–2030 Organization Green Climate Fund (GCF) Opportunity type Indigenous Peoples advisory/governance nomination Term 2027–2030 Vacancies Four regional vacancies Africa One vacancy Eastern Europe and Central Asia One vacancy Latin America and the Caribbean One vacancy Pacific One vacancy Nominees Indigenous Peoples representatives Geographic focus Developing States where GCF may fund activities Who submits Indigenous Peoples institutions, bodies and organizations Selection approach Indigenous Peoples-led self-selection process Membership Voluntary and non-remunerated Meetings Two in-person meetings annually and monthly online meetings Working language English Travel Travel-related arrangements may be supported for required in-person participation under applicable GCF policies Additional endorsements Highly encouraged Deadline 9 October 2026 Submission email IPAGnomination@gcfund.org Important Documents to Review The Green Climate Fund has published two principal documents associated with this call: Main Call for Nominations – provides the details of the 2027–2030 nomination process, regional vacancies, nomination requirements, and submission deadline. IPAG Terms of Reference – provides the framework covering the role and functions of IPAG, membership, competencies and factors to be considered, self-selection, working arrangements, and other provisions. Potential nominators should review both documents carefully before preparing their submission. Conclusion The Green Climate Fund Indigenous Peoples Advisory Group 2027–2030 call for nominations provides an institutional pathway for Indigenous Peoples representatives to contribute to engagement between Indigenous Peoples, the Green Climate Fund, and its partners. The opportunity is particularly distinctive because it is not structured as a conventional job, fellowship, scholarship, or individual application. title: FCDO Research Advisory Group 2026: Part-Time Remote Opportunity for Senior Global Research and Policy Experts
summary: The FCDO Research Advisory Group (RAG) is seeking experienced experts to join its advisory group and provide independent scientific and research advice to the UK Foreign, Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO) . This is a senior-level, part-time advisory opportunity for individuals with substantial expertise in areas such as health, agriculture, climate, energy, water, economic growth, humanitarian affairs, education, governance, conflict, social development, data for development, big data and artificial intelligence . Members will contribute strategic advice on FCDO s research priorities, funding portfolio, evidence use, research quality, value for money, emerging global challenges and connections with the wider UK and international research community. The position is remote, part-time and unremunerated , although FCDO will reimburse reasonable economy travel and incidental expenses associated with the role. About the FCDO Research Advisory Group The FCDO Research Advisory Group was established in 2022 to provide strategic guidance, rapid insight and independent challenge to FCDO s research funding portfolio. The Group supports the work of the FCDO Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA) , who is also the Director of the Research and Evidence Division. Its role is to help assure the quality, relevance and appropriateness of FCDO s research portfolio . The Group brings together experts with thematic and geographic knowledge covering a wide range of global development and international policy issues. Its areas of expertise include: Health Agriculture Climate Energy Water Economic growth Humanitarian affairs Education Governance Conflict Social development Data for development Big data Artificial intelligence Innovation and related research areas Members are expected to contribute their expertise while also engaging with issues that extend beyond their own individual academic discipline. What Is the Role of an FCDO Research Advisory Group Member? Members provide independent scientific and research advice to FCDO . The role is not simply about advising on an individual s specialist field. Members are appointed in a personal capacity , meaning they serve as independent experts rather than representatives of their employer, profession, institution or an interest group. Members are also expected to contribute across the Group s broader agenda. Their responsibilities include providing insight into how research and evidence can support international development and wider foreign policy objectives. Key Responsibilities 1. Advising on FCDO Research Priorities Members will contribute to discussions concerning: FCDO s research priorities Research activities The relationship between FCDO research and the wider UK science base Connections with international research communities Emerging areas where additional research may be required Their advice can help FCDO consider whether its research portfolio is addressing important global challenges and research needs. 2. Supporting Evidence-Informed Policy A central responsibility of the Group is helping ensure that FCDO policy is informed by the best available research and evidence . Members may therefore be asked to consider the quality, relevance and usefulness of research being used to inform policy. This requires an understanding of how research can be translated into practical policy and development impact. 3. Reviewing Research Programme Effectiveness Members will comment on the: Effectiveness of research programmes Value for money of research investments Funding mechanisms for research and development Performance and relevance of research activities This means applicants should be able to engage with questions concerning not only academic quality but also the practical impact and effectiveness of research funding. 4. Advising on the Research Portfolio Members will help assess the overall balance and adequacy of FCDO s research portfolio. This includes identifying: Research gaps Areas requiring greater attention Areas that may deserve less emphasis Emerging research priorities Opportunities for strengthening the overall portfolio Members therefore need to be able to think beyond individual research projects and consider research strategically at portfolio level. 5. Horizon-Scanning and Scenario Planning The Group also participates in horizon-scanning and long-range scenario planning . This involves considering emerging global challenges and developments that could have implications for research, international development and policy. Experts should therefore be comfortable thinking about future trends and possible challenges rather than focusing exclusively on current issues. 6. Connecting FCDO With Specialist Expertise Members can provide advice and connections to specialist expertise across: The UK research community International research institutions Academic networks Relevant specialist fields Global research communities Their networks and understanding of the international research environment can therefore contribute to the Group s advisory role. 7. title: Morgan Stanley 2027 Investment Management Sophomore Summer Analyst Program in New York: Private Credit & Equity Internship

Morgan Stanley maintains a global presence and states that its employees work across 41 countries , with opportunities available to students and graduates in different regions. Team: Tactical Value Successful participants will join the Tactical Value team . This provides Summer Analysts with an opportunity to learn about how investment professionals examine potential investments, conduct research, assess companies and industries, evaluate financial information, and contribute to the investment process. Due diligence involves gathering and analyzing information about a prospective investment so that investment professionals can better understand its financial position, business model, industry, risks, opportunities, and overall investment characteristics. This responsibility can help students develop their ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally. Skills that may be developed include: Written communication Investment research Data interpretation Company analysis Industry analysis Presentation of findings Attention to detail Business writing 6. Participants can therefore gain insight into portfolio management and ongoing investment analysis. 7. Depending on the position, compensation may also include other forms of compensation and benefits, such as: Incentive compensation Discretionary bonuses Commission earnings where applicable Other short- and long-term incentive packages Morgan Stanley-sponsored benefit programs The exact compensation package should be confirmed through the official employment documentation and applicable terms for the position. title: EU Delegation Vienna Funded Traineeships 2027: Paid Opportunities for Young Graduates in International Relations, Diplomacy and Global Affairs
summary: Are you a young graduate interested in international relations, diplomacy, European affairs, international organisations, security, human rights or multilateral cooperation? The European Union Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna is offering funded traineeships for young graduates across several sections of its diplomatic mission. These traineeships provide an opportunity to gain practical experience inside an EU Delegation and to observe how the European Union represents its interests and values within international organisations based in Vienna. The 2027 traineeship call covers several areas, including the United Nations Section, OSCE Section, Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section, and Administrative/Head of Delegation Section . The traineeships can last for up to six months , subject to budget availability, with the earliest anticipated start in March 2027 and a possible additional intake during the second semester of 2027. The application deadline is 30 September 2026 . Successful trainees receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses , although applicants should note that travel, visa, insurance and accommodation costs are to be borne by the trainee. This opportunity is particularly relevant for graduates who want to build experience in European foreign policy, diplomacy, international organisations, multilateral affairs, international security, human rights, nuclear non-proliferation, public diplomacy or EU external action. About the EU Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna The European Union maintains a Delegation in Vienna that works with several major international organisations headquartered or represented in the city. Vienna is an important centre for multilateral diplomacy and international cooperation. Organisations and institutions connected to the Delegation s work include bodies such as the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, United Nations Industrial Development Organization, United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs, United Nations Commission on International Trade Law, Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, International Atomic Energy Agency and other international organisations. The traineeship therefore provides exposure to an environment where international policy, diplomacy, security, development, human rights, international law and multilateral negotiations intersect. The current call was published by the European External Action Service on 15 September 2026 as a new opportunity. What the Funded Traineeship Offers The EU Delegation is offering traineeships of up to six months , subject to budget availability. The tentative starting period is the first semester of 2027 , with the earliest possible starting date being March 2027 . Depending on availability, traineeships may also begin during the second semester of 2027. Selected trainees will receive a monthly traineeship grant intended to cover living expenses . The EEAS notes that the amount may be updated before the traineeship begins, meaning applicants should not assume that a particular historical grant amount will apply to the 2027 intake. However, the financial support does not mean that every cost associated with relocating to Vienna will be covered. Applicants are responsible for: Travel costs. Visa costs where applicable. Insurance costs. Accommodation costs. Other expenses that are not covered by the traineeship grant. Candidates should therefore consider the full cost of living in Vienna and their personal financial circumstances before accepting a traineeship. Traineeship Sections Available The 2027 call covers several sections of the EU Delegation. Applicants can express interest in one traineeship per delegation , although the Delegation states that, depending on an applicant s profile, it may offer a traineeship in another section. The sections include: United Nations Section OSCE Section Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section Administrative and Head of Delegation Section Each section offers a different type of professional experience. 1. Traineeship in the United Nations Section The UN Section supports the Head of Delegation in the role of Ambassador of the European Union towards international organisations based in Vienna. The section works across a broad multilateral agenda involving organisations and topics including: UNODC UNIDO UNOOSA UNCITRAL Drugs and crime Outer space Industrial development Multilateral cooperation EU statements and positions Outreach to international organisations Relations with third countries Public diplomacy The section also prepares reports and information for the European External Action Service and the European Commission . This makes the UN traineeship particularly relevant to graduates interested in diplomacy, international organisations, European foreign policy, multilateralism, international development, international law and global governance. Main Tasks in the UN Section Trainees may assist permanent staff with: Preparing meetings and diplomatic activities. Drafting briefings. Preparing reports. Drafting statements and other official documents. Participating in meetings. Taking notes during meetings. Supporting public diplomacy activities. These responsibilities can help trainees develop practical skills in diplomatic writing, policy analysis, meeting reporting and international relations. 2. Traineeship in the OSCE Section The OSCE Section supports the Deputy Head of Delegation in her role as EU Ambassador to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe. The OSCE s work covers three broad dimensions of security: Politico-military security. Economic and environmental security. Human rights and fundamental freedoms. The section follows a wide range of regional and thematic issues. The current notice identifies Russia s war of aggression against Ukraine as an important part of the organisation s current agenda, alongside issues such as: Trafficking in human beings. Transnational threats. Economic and environmental aspects of security. Human rights. Fundamental freedoms. Regional political developments. The section represents the EU at OSCE meetings and events, prepares and coordinates EU statements and messages, engages with third countries and prepares reports and briefings for the EEAS and EU institutions. It also conducts public diplomacy activities highlighting EU achievements. Main Tasks in the OSCE Section A trainee may be expected to: Monitor developments across the OSCE s three security dimensions. Attend OSCE meetings with permanent staff. Support work on regional and thematic dossiers. Assist with EU coordination and outreach activities. Help draft and review EU statements and messages. Take notes during OSCE and EU meetings. Prepare reports on meetings and consultations. Conduct background research on EU and OSCE topics. Support public diplomacy activities. This section is particularly relevant to graduates interested in international security, European security policy, conflict and peace studies, human rights, international relations and multilateral diplomacy. 3. Traineeship in the Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section The Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Section , abbreviated as NNP, deals with a specialised area of international security policy. Its work covers a dense multilateral agenda concerning nuclear issues and non-proliferation. The section follows activities involving the: International Atomic Energy Agency. Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization. Nuclear safety. Nuclear security. Nuclear safeguards. Technical cooperation. Non-proliferation. Export controls. Nuclear-related international negotiations. The current notice specifically refers to issues involving Ukraine, Iran, the Democratic People s Republic of Korea and Syria, as well as nuclear safety, security and safeguards. The section also coordinates the EU s contribution to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty process. Main Tasks in the NNP Section Trainees may assist permanent staff with: Preparing meetings. Supporting diplomatic activities. Drafting briefings. Preparing reports. Drafting statements. Participating in meetings. Taking meeting notes. Supporting public diplomacy activities. This traineeship can be particularly relevant to graduates interested in international security, nuclear policy, non-proliferation, international organisations, diplomacy, international law and European foreign and security policy. 4. Administrative and Head of Delegation Section The fourth area combines work connected to the Administrative Section and the Head of Delegation Section . This opportunity is different from the specialist political traineeships because the requirements are different. For the ADMIN section, a Bachelor s degree in a relevant discipline is sufficient , while candidates also need B2 German language skills . Policy-document drafting experience is not required for this section, but numeracy is considered essential. Administrative Section The Administrative Section is responsible for essential operational processes that allow the Delegation to function effectively. Its responsibilities include areas such as: Financial management. Budget management. Procurement. Document archiving. Protocol matters. Liaison with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. VAT exemption processes. Diplomatic cards. Administrative coordination. Head of Delegation Section The Head of Delegation Section provides strategic and organisational support to the EU Ambassador. Its work includes: Internal coordination. Policy coordination across Delegation sections. High-level diplomatic visits. High-level meetings. Formal events. Social events. Official correspondence. Agenda management. Press relations. Public diplomacy. Cultural diplomacy. Digital communication. Website management. Social media. Public events and campaigns. Team Europe coordination. Administrative and financial tasks. Main Tasks for ADMIN/HoD Trainees A trainee may assist with: General administrative and office tasks. Protocol activities. Updating internal guides. Updating contact lists. Maintaining distribution lists. Meeting and visit logistics. Representation activities. Social events. Creating social media content. Updating the Delegation website. Payment files. Archiving. Ad hoc administrative requests. This section may therefore be particularly useful for graduates interested in diplomacy, administration, communications, protocol, public diplomacy, event management and international institutional operations. Before applying, you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship). Source: https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/vienna-international-organisations/funded-traineeships-young-graduates-eu-delegation-international-organisations-vienna-multiple_en?s=66 Who Is Eligible to Apply? The eligibility requirements differ slightly depending on the section. For the UN, OSCE and Nuclear and Non-Proliferation sections, the Vienna call specifies that applicants must hold a Master s degree in a relevant discipline . Candidates without a Master s degree are explicitly stated to be ineligible for these traineeships. Relevant academic backgrounds include: International Politics. European Studies. International Relations. International Law. International Economics. Related disciplines connected to international affairs. For the ADMIN section, a relevant Bachelor s degree is sufficient. Academic Requirements by Section Section Minimum qualification UN Relevant Master s degree OSCE Relevant Master s degree Nuclear and Non-Proliferation Relevant Master s degree ADMIN/HoD Relevant Bachelor s degree Applicants should therefore select their preferred section carefully and verify that they meet the specific academic requirement. Professional Experience Requirement Candidates must have less than one year of professional experience after graduation by the time the traineeship agreement is signed . This makes the opportunity particularly suitable for recent graduates who have completed their studies and are beginning their professional careers. The EEAS general framework similarly establishes a maximum of one year of professional experience after graduation for the funded young-graduate traineeship pillar. Applicants should therefore calculate their post-graduation professional experience carefully rather than assuming that being a recent graduate automatically makes them eligible. Previous Experience in EU Institutions Applicants must not have more than six weeks of previous experience in EU Institutions . This restriction applies to previous training or employment in EU institutions and is part of the broader EEAS traineeship framework. Candidates who have already accumulated more than the permitted period should review the rules carefully before submitting an application. Language Requirements Excellent English-language skills are required for the specialist sections. The call specifically highlights English proficiency because trainees will be working in an international diplomatic environment involving meetings, policy documents, reports, statements and international organisations. Additional language abilities can strengthen a candidate s profile. The Vienna notice indicates that experience working in other OSCE languages and the ability to work in other UN languages would be an asset. For the ADMIN section , B2-level German is specifically required. Therefore, language expectations can be summarised as follows: UN: Excellent English; additional relevant languages are an asset. OSCE: Excellent English; OSCE-language skills are an asset. NNP: Excellent English; additional international working languages can be beneficial. ADMIN: B2 German is required. Additional Skills and Experience That Can Strengthen an Application The Vienna Delegation is looking for candidates with demonstrated interest in the EU s external action and international relations. For the specialist sections, relevant areas include: Security. Human rights. International organisations. The United Nations. European foreign policy. International diplomacy. Multilateral affairs. Applicants should also have experience in: Drafting policy documents. Taking meeting notes. Drafting meeting reports. Conducting background research. Preparing written briefings. Previous experience with an international organisation or diplomatic mission is considered an asset, although the notice does not state that this experience is mandatory for every applicant. What Are the Benefits of the Traineeship? The opportunity provides several forms of professional and educational value. 1. Monthly Financial Grant Selected trainees receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses . The EEAS notes that the grant information may be updated before the traineeship begins. Applicants should therefore consult the latest official financial information when preparing for the traineeship. 2. Practical Diplomatic Experience The traineeship provides exposure to the daily work of an EU diplomatic mission. Depending on the selected section, trainees can gain experience with: Diplomatic meetings. International organisations. Policy research. Briefing preparation. EU statements. Reporting. Public diplomacy. International security. Administrative operations. Communications. 3. Exposure to International Organisations Vienna is an important centre for multilateral diplomacy. Trainees in the UN, OSCE and NNP sections can gain practical exposure to the work of international organisations and the processes through which governments and international institutions address global issues. 4. Professional Writing Experience Several traineeship tasks involve producing professional documents. These can include: Briefing notes. Reports. Statements. Meeting records. Research summaries. Other diplomatic documents. This can help graduates strengthen their policy-writing and analytical skills. 5. Networking and Professional Exposure Working inside an EU Delegation can expose trainees to diplomats, EU officials, international organisations, government representatives and professionals working on international policy. This can help trainees understand the professional environment of international affairs. 6. Public Diplomacy Experience Several sections engage in public diplomacy. Trainees may support: Public events. Communications activities. Social media. Website updates. Campaigns. Visibility activities. This is particularly relevant to applicants interested in strategic communication and international public diplomacy. What Costs Does the Trainee Need to Cover? Although the opportunity is funded through a monthly grant, the financial arrangement does not mean that all expenses are covered. The official notice states that travel, visa, insurance and accommodation costs must be borne by the trainee . Applicants should therefore prepare a realistic budget that considers: Accommodation in Vienna. Transportation. Food and daily living expenses. Visa costs where applicable. Insurance. Travel to and from Vienna. Personal expenses. The monthly grant is intended to contribute toward living expenses, but applicants should not assume it will automatically cover every cost. How to Apply for the EU Delegation Vienna Traineeship Applications must be submitted by email. The designated email address is: Delegation-Vienna-Trainees@eeas.europa.eu Applicants must provide three key documents. 1. Europass Curriculum Vitae The Delegation requires a detailed standard Europass CV . Importantly, the notice states that CVs in other formats will not be considered. Applicants should therefore use the official Europass format rather than sending a conventional personal résumé: https://europa.eu/europass/en 2. Cover Letter Applicants must submit a cover letter explaining why they want to participate in an EU traineeship. The cover letter should be specific to the opportunity. Candidates should explain: Why they are interested in the EU. Why they are interested in international relations. Why they selected the relevant section. What academic experience they bring. What relevant professional or research experience they have. How their skills relate to the traineeship. What they hope to learn. 3. Application Form Applicants must also complete the official application form provided with the vacancy notice. The current application form is titled: Austria UN OSCE Vienna Application form for multiple funded traineeships 2027 Candidates should download and complete the correct form before submitting their application. Important Email Subject Requirement Applicants must use the required email subject line. The subject should follow the format: Funded Traineeship – Your Name/Acronym of the Section This requirement is important because the Delegation states that applications without the specified subject line will not be considered . Candidates should therefore avoid using generic subject lines such as: Traineeship Application Application EU Internship Vienna Internship Instead, they should follow the format requested by the Delegation. One Application Per Delegation Candidates may apply for only one traineeship per Delegation . However, the Delegation states that based on an applicant s profile, it could offer the candidate a traineeship in another section. Applicants should therefore select the section that best matches their: Academic qualifications. Professional interests. Language skills. Research experience. Career objectives. Previous international affairs experience. Application Deadline The deadline for the EU Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna funded traineeships is: 30 September 2026 The opportunity is listed by the EEAS as a Trainee position in Vienna. Because applications must be submitted by email, candidates should avoid waiting until the final day. Preparing the Europass CV, cover letter and application form in advance can reduce the risk of submitting an incomplete application. Selection Process The Delegation will evaluate the applications after the deadline. According to the official notice: Applications are evaluated. Shortlisted candidates are contacted. Shortlisted candidates are invited for an interview. Successful candidates must provide the required documentation. Candidates who cannot provide required documentation may have their application rejected. Unsuccessful candidates are notified by email. Candidates should therefore monitor the email address used in their application after submission. Nationality and Geographic Eligibility The EEAS general framework states that funded traineeships in EU Delegations can be open to: Citizens of EU Member States. Citizens of EU candidate countries that have signed an accession agreement with the EU. Citizens of the host country, depending on the relevant traineeship pillar and applicable rules. The specific Vienna notice additionally contains requirements concerning documentation for citizens of EU Member States , including proof of appropriate coverage and relevant visa or temporary residence documentation where applicable. Because nationality rules can depend on the specific traineeship framework and host-country legislation, candidates should verify their individual eligibility against the latest EEAS rules before applying. The opportunity should therefore not be assumed to be open to applicants from every country worldwide. Requirements for EU Citizens The Vienna notice states that citizens of EU Member States must: Provide proof of coverage against the risk of a pandemic and repatriation costs. Hold a relevant entrance visa and/or temporary residence permit where applicable. Ensure that these documents comply with the traineeship agreement and local legislation. These requirements should be reviewed carefully by selected candidates before the traineeship begins. Compliance With Local and National Legislation The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with: Austrian legislation. Applicable EU rules. The legislation of the trainee s country of origin. Relevant visa and residence requirements. The terms of the traineeship agreement. Applicants should therefore understand that meeting the academic and professional requirements alone does not necessarily resolve immigration or legal requirements. How to Prepare a Strong Application Although selection is competitive, applicants can improve the clarity and relevance of their application by carefully matching their profile to the selected section. Step 1: Choose One Section Carefully Do not apply indiscriminately. Consider whether your background fits: UN and multilateral diplomacy. OSCE and international security. Nuclear and non-proliferation affairs. Administration and diplomatic support. Step 2: Tailor Your Europass CV The CV should make relevant experience easy to identify. Highlight: Academic qualifications. Policy research. International relations experience. Diplomatic or international organisation exposure. Writing experience. Research skills. Meeting and reporting experience. Language skills. Relevant publications. Relevant internships. Relevant volunteering or extracurricular activities. Step 3: Make the Cover Letter Specific Avoid sending a generic cover letter that could be used for any internship. Explain why you are interested in: The EU Delegation. Vienna. The specific section. International organisations. EU external action. The relevant policy area. Step 4: Demonstrate Writing Ability Many of the tasks involve drafting reports, briefings, statements and other documents. Candidates should therefore demonstrate their ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally. Step 5: Show Relevant Research Experience The OSCE section, for example, requires background research on EU and OSCE-related issues. Applicants should demonstrate that they can: Locate reliable information. Analyse policy developments. Summarise complex issues. Identify relevant developments. Produce concise written outputs. Step 6: Check the Email Subject This is particularly important because the notice explicitly states that applications without the required subject line will not be considered. Step 7: Submit the Complete Application Before sending the email, verify that it contains: Europass CV. Cover letter. Completed application form. Correct subject line. Correct recipient email address. Learn More HERE Why Vienna Is an Important Location for This Opportunity Vienna provides a particularly relevant environment for graduates interested in international affairs. The city hosts several major international organisations and multilateral institutions, making it an important centre for diplomacy and international cooperation. The Delegation s work connects European Union policy with international organisations dealing with: Security. Nuclear issues. Non-proliferation. Human rights. International development. Drugs and crime. Industrial development. Outer space. International trade and law. Multilateral cooperation. A traineeship in this environment can therefore expose young graduates to the practical workings of international diplomacy rather than limiting them to classroom-based study. Key Facts at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity EU Delegation Vienna Funded Traineeships Organisation European External Action Service / EU Delegation Location Vienna, Austria Duration Up to 6 months Expected start First semester 2027; earliest March 2027 Sections UN, OSCE, Nuclear and Non-Proliferation, ADMIN/HoD Funding Monthly grant for living expenses Travel Paid by trainee Visa Paid by trainee Insurance Paid by trainee Accommodation Paid by trainee Deadline 30 September 2026 Application method Email Required CV Europass format Cover letter Required Application form Required Maximum prior EU institutional experience 6 weeks Post-graduation professional experience Less than 1 year The details above are based on the current EEAS vacancy notice. Official Application Information Applicants should consult the official EEAS vacancy before submitting their application, particularly the detailed general eligibility rules for paid traineeships and any requirements related to nationality, immigration, insurance and local legislation. The official vacancy is available on the European External Action Service website . The EEAS also provides a general explanation of traineeships in EU Delegations, including the different traineeship pillars, nationality requirements, diploma requirements and restrictions on previous EU institutional experience. Conclusion The EU Delegation to the International Organisations in Vienna Funded Traineeships 2027 provide young graduates with an opportunity to gain practical experience in European diplomacy, international relations and multilateral affairs. The programme offers placements across several specialised areas, including the United Nations, OSCE, Nuclear and Non-Proliferation, and Administrative/Head of Delegation sections. Depending on the section, trainees can participate in diplomatic meetings, conduct policy research, draft reports and statements, support public diplomacy, contribute to communications activities and assist with the organisation of international events. For the specialist political and international affairs sections, applicants need a relevant Master s degree, while the ADMIN section accepts a relevant Bachelor s degree and requires B2 German. Candidates must also have less than one year of professional experience after graduation and must not have more than six weeks of previous experience in EU institutions. Selected trainees receive a monthly grant for living expenses, but they are responsible for travel, visa, insurance and accommodation costs. Candidates should therefore evaluate both the professional benefits and the financial requirements before accepting the opportunity. The application deadline is 30 September 2026 . Interested candidates should prepare a detailed Europass CV, a tailored cover letter and the required application form and submit them to Delegation-Vienna-Trainees@eeas.europa.eu using the prescribed email subject line. For graduates seeking early professional experience in diplomacy, international organisations, European foreign policy, security, human rights, non-proliferation, public diplomacy or international administration, the Vienna traineeship provides a direct opportunity to learn how an EU diplomatic mission operates within a major multilateral environment.
