title: Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027: Up to £70,000 for Experienced Researchers in Any Discipline
summary: The Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 provide funding for experienced researchers who need dedicated time to complete a programme of original research. The scheme is particularly aimed at researchers whose routine teaching and administrative responsibilities have limited their ability to undertake research in recent years. The fellowship offers up to £70,000 and can support research periods lasting between 3 and 24 months . Researchers from a wide range of academic disciplines can apply, making this an opportunity for established scholars seeking protected time to develop and complete substantial research projects. About the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships The Research Fellowships are offered by the Leverhulme Trust , a UK charitable organisation that supports research and education. The fellowship is designed around a specific challenge faced by many experienced academics: although they may have strong research ideas and established research records, their ability to conduct research can be restricted by teaching, administration and other routine institutional responsibilities. The programme therefore provides financial support that can enable successful applicants to devote a significant period of time to their research. The Trust gives particular priority to applicants whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly affected their capacity to conduct research during the three years before applying . This makes the fellowship especially relevant to experienced researchers who can demonstrate that institutional responsibilities have prevented them from giving sufficient attention to an important original research programme. Fellowship Value Successful applicants can receive funding of up to: £70,000 The maximum value gives researchers substantial flexibility to structure an appropriate period of research leave and cover eligible costs associated with undertaking the proposed research. Applicants should nevertheless ensure that their requested budget is appropriate to the scale and requirements of their proposed project rather than simply requesting the maximum amount available. Duration of the Fellowship Research Fellowships can be held for: A minimum of 3 months Up to a maximum of 24 months The duration should correspond to the amount of dedicated research time genuinely required to complete the proposed programme. A project requiring a shorter period of concentrated research may therefore be proposed for a shorter fellowship, while a more substantial programme may require a longer period, subject to the scheme s conditions and assessment. Who Is the Fellowship Designed For? The Research Fellowships are intended for experienced researchers who want to complete a defined piece or programme of original research. The scheme is particularly relevant to researchers who: Have an established research background. Have developed an original research project that requires dedicated time to complete. Have been unable to devote sufficient time to research because of routine academic responsibilities. Have significant teaching commitments. Have substantial administrative responsibilities within their institution. Can demonstrate that these responsibilities have affected their research activity during the three years preceding the application. Are able to undertake the proposed research within the fellowship period. The Trust s emphasis on the impact of teaching and administration means that applicants should clearly explain how their professional responsibilities have constrained their research time and why the fellowship would make a meaningful difference. Research in Any Discipline One of the notable features of the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowship is its broad disciplinary scope. The opportunity is available to researchers working across disciplines rather than being restricted to a single academic field. Depending on the nature of the proposed project, this can include research areas within fields such as: Humanities Social sciences Arts and related disciplines Natural sciences Other eligible academic research fields The breadth of the scheme means that the quality and originality of the proposed research, together with the applicant s experience and eligibility, are important considerations. Applicants should consult the official scheme guidance carefully to determine whether their particular discipline and research proposal satisfy the Trust s requirements. Why the Fellowship Is Important for Experienced Researchers Academic researchers often have responsibilities extending well beyond conducting research. Teaching, student supervision, administration, committee responsibilities, institutional projects and other duties can substantially reduce the amount of time available for original research. The Leverhulme Research Fellowship is structured to address this problem by providing support for a period in which an experienced researcher can concentrate on a specific research programme. For an applicant, the fellowship may therefore provide an opportunity to: Create dedicated research time The fellowship can help an experienced researcher obtain a sustained period away from routine responsibilities so that they can concentrate on their research. Complete an existing research programme Researchers who have already developed a substantial body of work but have struggled to bring it to completion may use the fellowship period to make significant progress. Develop original research The scheme is intended for original research, making the research question, methodology and anticipated contribution important elements of an application. Advance an established research career A successful fellowship can provide researchers with additional time and resources to develop significant scholarly work. Address research interruptions caused by academic duties Researchers whose teaching and administrative workload has reduced their research capacity can explain this context as part of their application. Priority for Researchers Affected by Teaching and Administrative Duties A particularly important feature of this fellowship is the Trust s stated priority for applicants whose research has been affected by routine institutional responsibilities. The Trust specifically indicates that priority will be given to applicants whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly impacted their ability to undertake research during the three years before the application . This means applicants should pay close attention to explaining their circumstances. Rather than simply stating that they are busy, applicants should demonstrate the relationship between their professional workload and their reduced research activity. For example, an applicant may need to explain: The nature of their teaching responsibilities. The extent of their administrative workload. How these responsibilities have affected their available research time. The period over which the impact occurred. How dedicated fellowship time would allow them to complete the proposed research. The purpose should be to establish a clear connection between the applicant s current circumstances and the need for the fellowship. What Type of Research Can Be Proposed? The fellowship is intended to support a piece or programme of original research . Consequently, applicants should have a clearly defined research objective rather than presenting a general desire to undertake academic work. A strong proposal should communicate: The central research question or problem. The significance of the research. The originality of the proposed work. The approach or methodology to be used. The work that will be undertaken during the fellowship. The expected scholarly contribution. Why the proposed fellowship period is necessary. How the research will progress during the requested period. The research programme should also be realistically structured around the amount of time and funding requested. Internationally Focused Projects The fellowship information also contains guidance concerning projects with an international focus . Researchers whose proposed work involves international subjects, locations, sources, collaborations or comparative research should carefully review the Trust s specific guidance on projects with an international focus before submitting an application. This is particularly important for researchers whose projects extend beyond the UK or involve research activities in multiple countries. Applicants should make sure that the international dimension of their proposal is clearly justified by the research itself and that all relevant eligibility and funding conditions are satisfied. Application Preparation The Leverhulme Trust advises prospective applicants to read the available information before beginning the application. The Trust has provided Application Help Notes 2027 to assist researchers in preparing their submissions. The guidance should be reviewed carefully because it contains information about the requirements and information applicants need to prepare. Applicants should ideally begin preparation well before the closing date, allowing enough time to develop their research proposal, assemble supporting information and review their application before submission. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the Leverhulme Grant System . Prospective applicants should: Review the Research Fellowships information provided by the Leverhulme Trust. Read the Application Help Notes 2027 . Develop a clearly defined original research programme. Confirm that they meet the fellowship s eligibility requirements. Consider the appropriate duration of the proposed fellowship. Prepare the information and supporting material required by the application system. Prepare a realistic funding request, taking into account the maximum fellowship value. Submit the completed application through the Leverhulme Grant System before the deadline. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit, particularly where institutional approval or additional information may be required. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline for the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 is: 5 November 2026 Applicants should ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated closing date and should check the official application system for any submission-time requirements. Funding Amount and Duration at a Glance Feature Details Fellowship Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 Maximum value £70,000 Fellowship duration 3 to 24 months Research area Any discipline, subject to scheme eligibility Target applicants Experienced researchers Particular priority Researchers whose teaching and administrative duties have significantly affected research during the previous three years Research focus Original research Deadline 5 November 2026 Application system Leverhulme Grant System What Applicants Should Emphasise Applicants should ensure that their proposal presents a convincing and coherent explanation of the research they intend to undertake. Several areas deserve particular attention. 1. Explain the originality of the research The application should make clear what is new about the proposed research and what contribution it is expected to make. 2. Demonstrate research experience Because the fellowship is intended for experienced researchers, applicants should present their relevant research background and demonstrate their ability to undertake the proposed work. 3. Explain the need for dedicated research time Applicants should clearly explain why the research cannot easily be completed alongside their existing teaching and administrative responsibilities. 4. Address the three-year context Researchers who have been significantly affected by teaching and administrative responsibilities should clearly explain how those duties have constrained their research activities during the relevant three-year period. 5. Develop a realistic timetable The proposed research should be achievable within the requested fellowship period. Applicants should demonstrate how the available research time will be used. 6. Prepare an appropriate budget Although the maximum award is £70,000, applicants should request an amount that is justified by the needs of their specific research programme. Research Fellowship Application Strategy A prospective applicant can strengthen the preparation process by treating the application as a coherent research case rather than simply a request for funding. The application should connect four central elements: Research problem → Original contribution → Need for dedicated time → Achievable research programme The research problem establishes what the applicant wants to investigate. The originality explains why the research matters academically. The explanation of the applicant s workload establishes why dedicated fellowship time is necessary. Finally, the research plan demonstrates that the proposed work can realistically be completed during the fellowship. This structure can help ensure that the application remains focused and that the need for fellowship support is clearly communicated. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is designed for experienced researchers . The information provided by the Leverhulme Trust does not describe the fellowship as a general scholarship for undergraduate or newly enrolled students. Applicants should therefore assess their level of research experience and their ability to demonstrate a substantive programme of original research. The Trust s emphasis on applicants affected by teaching and administrative responsibilities also means that the fellowship is particularly relevant to established researchers working within academic or research institutions. Who Is Not the Main Target of the Fellowship? Based on the stated purpose of the scheme, this opportunity is not primarily presented as a general funding programme for: Undergraduate students. Students seeking tuition funding. Applicants without an established research background. Individuals seeking general professional development funding. Projects that are not based on original research. The fellowship is specifically framed around experienced researchers seeking time to complete a programme of original research. Official Application Resources Prospective applicants should review the Leverhulme Trust s official Research Fellowships information and the Application Help Notes 2027 before preparing their application. The application is made through the Leverhulme Grant System . The Trust also provides a dedicated contact for Research Fellowship enquiries, which applicants can use if their questions are not answered in the published guidance. Visit HERE for more information about the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027. Conclusion The Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowships 2027 offer experienced researchers an opportunity to obtain dedicated time and financial support to complete original research. With funding of up to £70,000 and fellowship periods ranging from 3 to 24 months , the scheme can provide substantial support for researchers whose teaching and administrative responsibilities have limited their ability to pursue research. The fellowship is particularly relevant to applicants who can demonstrate that their routine academic duties have significantly affected their research capacity during the previous three years. Researchers should therefore carefully explain their research experience, the originality and importance of their proposed project, the effect of their existing responsibilities, and why a dedicated fellowship period is necessary. Interested researchers should begin preparing early, read the 2027 application guidance carefully and submit their applications through the Leverhulme Grant System before the 5 November 2026 deadline. title: EBRD Internship 2026 in Brussels: Apply for a 6-Month Intern Position in Corporate Strategy
summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is inviting applications for an Intern position based in Brussels, Belgium , offering an opportunity for qualified graduates and early-career professionals to gain practical experience within an international financial institution. The six-month internship is situated within the Corporate Strategy Division and will involve work related to European Union policies and initiatives, institutional communications, policy engagement, events, meetings, research, and coordination. This EBRD internship provides an opportunity for an individual with an academic degree and some professional working experience to contribute to the work of the Bank s EU Representative Office while developing professional experience in an international and multicultural environment. The position may be particularly relevant to candidates interested in European Union affairs, international development, public policy, international organisations, communications, sustainability, finance, and institutional relations . Overview of the EBRD Internship Opportunity The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is recruiting an Intern to support its team in Brussels. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and contribute to a range of policy, communication, event, meeting, administrative, and coordination activities. According to the vacancy announcement, the internship has a duration of six months and is based in Brussels, Belgium. Key Opportunity Details Organisation: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) Position: Intern Division: Corporate Strategy Location: Brussels, Belgium Office Country: Belgium Office City: Brussels Contract Type: Internship Contract Length: 6 months Requisition ID: 37050 Posting Date: 11 September 2026 Application Deadline: 25 September 2026 The vacancy is designed for an individual who can support the Brussels-based team across policy engagement, communications, events, meetings, outreach, and coordination activities. About the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is an international financial institution that works across regions in which it invests. The organisation describes its approach as agile and innovative and highlights the opportunity for employees to work with experts from a wide range of professional sectors. Working at the EBRD can expose interns and other employees to professionals operating across areas including finance, public policy, international development, government, the private sector, and institutional relations. The organisation also places emphasis on values including: Inclusiveness Innovation Trust Responsibility These values are reflected in workplace behaviours that include listening and speaking up, collaborating, acting decisively, and simplifying processes to increase impact. For an intern interested in international organisations and development-related work, the environment can provide exposure to how an international financial institution interacts with policymakers, institutions, stakeholders, and other organisations. Purpose of the EBRD Brussels Internship The primary purpose of the position is to provide support to the Brussels team across several areas of work. The intern will work under the supervision of the Principal Manager and assist with activities connected to EU policies and initiatives, communications, policy engagement, outreach, events, meetings, administration, and project coordination . Because the role combines policy and communication responsibilities, applicants may benefit from having an interest in both the institutional and public-facing aspects of international development work. The position can therefore provide practical exposure to how policy developments are monitored, analysed, communicated, and incorporated into institutional engagement. Key Responsibilities of the EBRD Intern The selected candidate will be expected to support the team in several areas. 1. Supporting Analysis of EU Policies and Initiatives One of the key responsibilities will involve supporting the analysis of and engagement with European Union policies and initiatives . This means the intern will contribute to the team s understanding of relevant EU developments and help support engagement around policies and initiatives that may be relevant to the EBRD s work. This responsibility could provide valuable exposure to EU policymaking and the relationship between international financial institutions and European institutions. 2. Supporting Communication Activities The intern will also support internal and external communication activities aimed at raising the profile of the EBRD and its EU Representative Office. Communication responsibilities may involve helping the team communicate its activities, priorities, engagements, and work to relevant audiences. This part of the position may be particularly relevant to graduates and early-career professionals with an interest in corporate communications, public affairs, institutional communications, digital communication, or international development communication. 3. Attending Relevant Events The intern will have the opportunity to attend relevant events and report back to management. This responsibility can provide exposure to professional events involving policymakers, institutions, development organisations, financial-sector stakeholders, and other relevant actors. The ability to observe discussions, identify important developments, and communicate key information clearly will therefore be useful in this role. 4. Participating in Meetings The intern may participate in internal and external meetings where appropriate. This provides an opportunity to observe and contribute to professional discussions and gain insight into how an international organisation coordinates its work and engages with external stakeholders. 5. Supporting Policy Engagement and Communication Outreach Another important component of the internship involves supporting the team with both policy engagement and communication outreach . This combines two closely connected areas: understanding and engaging with policy developments while also helping communicate the organisation s work and priorities. Candidates who are comfortable researching information, preparing written materials, communicating professionally, and working with different stakeholders may find these responsibilities particularly relevant. 6. Administrative and Coordination Support The intern will also provide occasional administrative and coordination support for other project activities. Although these tasks may be secondary to the policy and communication responsibilities, they can be important for ensuring that projects and team activities are organised effectively. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail, reliability, and the ability to manage changing priorities can therefore be valuable. Academic and Professional Qualifications The EBRD states that applicants should have a degree with some professional working experience . The vacancy does not specify a single academic discipline in the information provided. Consequently, candidates from different educational backgrounds may potentially be relevant, particularly where their studies and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Relevant academic or professional interests may include areas such as: European studies International relations International development Public policy Political science Economics Finance Communications Corporate communications Public affairs Development studies Business International organisations Applicants should carefully review the official vacancy requirements before applying to determine whether their specific academic and professional background meets the employer s criteria. Professional Experience The vacancy requires candidates to have some professional working experience . The EBRD further notes that experience engaging with EU institutions or international organisations is a plus . This means previous experience in these environments can strengthen an applicant s relevance to the role, although the vacancy presents such experience as an advantage rather than as the stated core qualification. Experience gained through employment, internships, professional assignments, project work, or other relevant professional settings may help demonstrate an applicant s ability to operate in a structured organisational environment. Candidates should focus their application materials on experiences that demonstrate their ability to: Conduct research and analysis Understand policy developments Communicate professionally Work with different stakeholders Prepare or present information Support events and meetings Manage multiple tasks Coordinate activities Work independently Adapt to changing priorities Language Requirements Fluency in English is required for the position. Knowledge of French is an advantage . Because the role is located in Brussels and involves engagement connected to EU institutions and initiatives, language capabilities can be particularly useful when communicating in a multicultural and international environment. Applicants should clearly demonstrate their English-language proficiency and indicate any additional relevant language abilities in their application where appropriate. Knowledge of EU Institutions and Development Policy The EBRD is looking for candidates with knowledge of EU institutions and an understanding of development policy . This requirement is particularly relevant because a substantial part of the internship involves supporting the team s engagement with EU policies and initiatives. Applicants should therefore be familiar with the role and functions of relevant EU institutions and have an understanding of broader development-policy issues. A strong application should demonstrate genuine interest in the policy environment in which the EBRD operates rather than simply listing academic qualifications. Ability to Work Independently The successful candidate should be able to work independently while also understanding when it is appropriate to seek advice.
